correctness.rationale: For a selected a_i, self-privacy is J contained in {i}; an external witness b_j must satisfy j not in J, j different from i, and I minus {i} contained in {j}. The symmetric test is exact. Index overlap rules out every extension of a deleted pair. With disjoint nonempty indices there is no self-privacy, hence each side has size at most two. In a mixed triple the singleton needs an unused fourth index; in a disjoint (2,2) the other vertex on the same side supplies the index of an external witness. This proves the types, including the n=3 exception. Irredundance is hereditary. At n>=4 every disjoint mixed pair and triple extends to a (2,2) set, and none of the full sides, deleted pairs or disjoint (2,2) sets extends. At n=3 the full sides and all nine mixed pairs are maximal. The coefficients follow from counting these types; for example the quartic coefficient is binom(n,2)binom(n-2,2) plus the one-sided contribution when applicable. Both scalar invariants and the K_{n,n} comparison follow. Read VERIFICATION.md and verify_irredundance.py without running the frozen code; a separate direct closed-neighborhood enumeration over 3<=n<=7 corroborated both tables and maximality. At n=3 it obtained all-set coefficients 1,6,15,2 and maximal coefficients 9,2 in sizes 2,3; at n=4, (1,8,28,32,8) and 4x^2+8x^4. These bounded checks do not replace the local proof.

evidence: A290710 starts at crown n=3 with 24, then 77, and states size-resolved mixed type counts for n>3.
A289121 claims crown coverage for n>1 and starts 3,4,5,12 at offset 1, yielding a(3)=5. Its polynomial equals n+6 binom(n,4)+2 for n>=4.
A286954 has a(6)=11 for cycles. A291044 explicitly gives 9x^2+2x^3 in its row for cycle length six.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A289121's stated boundary value is contradicted by both the private-neighbor check and the equivalent cycle tables. This is not evidence that the correct boundary count was previously unknown.

originality.rationale: OEIS A290710 already states the entire all-set classification for n>=4 by the same types and their counts, including sizes of every mixed family, and separately lists the all-set total 24 at n=3. The graded enumerator is the size-weighted form of this classification. The n>=4 maximal families follow by one-vertex containment tests directly on those known types and A289121 lists their total. A289121 incorrectly lists 5 instead of 11 at crown order 3, but the correct count and the exact boundary polynomial 9x^2+2x^3 are already published under the equivalent cycle graph in A286954 and A291044. A narrow repair around the discrepancy would therefore be a reconciliation of known tables, not a distinct mathematical finding.
residual_risks: The 1979 Bollobás–Cockayne DOI and 2011 bipartite irredundance PDF did not yield open full text; they may contain broader coverage. The disposition rests on the verified same-object database entries, not access failures.
